text.p: The institutional tranche of Israel Discount Bank's share and warrants offering was 1.7 times oversubscribed, MI Holdings, the government company in charge of privatising Israel's banks, said on Monday.
Among foreign institutional investors Merrill Lynch bid for the largest amount -- 6.4 million shekels worth of shares and warrants, Meir Jacobson, managing director of MI Holdings, said.

The government, which holds 79 percent of Discount, is selling off 17 percent. MI Holdings will publish a prospectus on Tuesday and the second tranche of the offering, to the general public, is expected to take place next Monday.

In the first part, open only to institutional investors, the price was set at 160 shekels for a package of five shares, nine Series Two warrants (part of which are exercisable now and the rest in July) and seven Series Three warrants (exercisable in November).
The price was 2.6 percent above the minimum of 156 shekels but it could go even higher, depending on the results of next week's public offering.

The government expects to raise some 607 million shekels from the Discount sale -- 156 million from the public offering, 42 million from an issue to the bank's workers, 171 million from warrants exercised in July and 238 million in November.
The offering was to take place in February but was delayed after the Securities Authority asked to see more detailed information on the bank's fourth-quarter debt provision.
The government plans to float about 10 percent in Leumi, Israel's second largest bank, in May.
